transcript:
Header: 2026-10-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Aurora Bank), Ethan Cole (Aurora SRE), Jordan Reyes (Aurora ML)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's TTFT improvements; still seeing 60-80ms tail on upcalls with 256 seq; tried q4_0 and q4_1 with mixed results.

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check in before we dive in, is everyone good with the agenda?
[00:12] Priya Malhotra: yep all good, want to see the numbers and what changes we tried this week.
[00:22] Marcus Li: cool, i'll start with the microbench results we ran on Dedicated-like instance, note these are synthetic but aligned to last week's traces. link to perf sheet -> https://redwood.ai/sheets/aurorabank-perf
[00:37] Marcus Li: so baseline (no streaming, seq 256, batch size 8) avg TTFT ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 320ms; we then enabled streaming and continuous batching, avg TTFT dropped to ~60ms but p95 still around 140ms.
[01:05] Ethan Cole: those p99s are the thing we care about, our SLAs require <200ms for first token in 99.5% of calls.
[01:22] Jordan Reyes: and a lot of our requests are short — median seq len is 48 but we have a long tail to 512 for some analysis workflows.
[01:35] Speaker 2: (muffled) ok makes sense

[02:00] Marcus Li: wanted to call out kernel selection: on the Ampere-ish nodes we tried two kernels, default fused attention path vs optimized block attention. The optimized path helps for long sequences but has slightly higher cold start overhead, which hits TTFT.
[02:28] Priya Malhotra: by cold start overhead you mean JIT / kernel init time?
[02:33] Marcus Li: yeah it's the compilation and kernel warmup, plus some mem allocs. For Dedicated we can keep keepalive warm pools which reduces that, but for hosted-like bursty traffic it shows up.
[02:48] Lena Park: and to add, streaming helps user perceived latency because first token streams out before the whole decode, but it doesn't remove kernel init time.

[03:12] Jordan Reyes: curious about quantization — last week we tested q4_0 and q4_1, q4_0 was faster but occasionally produced tokenization artifacts, q4_1 was slightly slower but more stable. Any notes?
[03:30] Marcus Li: yep q4_0 tended to shave off ~10-15ms on avg TTFT, q4_1 was more conservative. With the block-attention kernel q4_1 actually matched q4_0 for some mid sequences. There's also a q5-ish profile in lab that we're not recommending yet.
[03:52] Ethan Cole: given our compliance needs, we also prefer minimal model changes; if q4_0 causes hallucinations we might reject it.

[04:20] Marcus Li: one more nuance: batching policy — we tested dynamic batching with 12ms waiting window vs 8ms. 12ms increased throughput but added 8-12ms to TTFT for small requests; 8ms kept TTFT lower but throughput down. It's classic latency vs cost tradeoff.
[04:48] Priya Malhotra: can we tie batching to request size? like tiny requests never wait, larger ones batch?
[04:55] Lena Park: yes that's supported — workload aware batching / size-based thresholds; SE can show config examples.

[06:00] Marcus Li: next i want to show a short clip of the perf trace (note: shared in chat). when we replayed realistic traces (Jordan's sample set from last week) we saw TTFT median ~52ms with streaming enabled and prior warm pools, p99 tightened to ~180ms. warm pools matter.
[06:28] Jordan Reyes: that matches our expectation, we just need to ensure warm pools don't blow our cost estimates.
[06:40] Marcus Li: totally — we estimated warm pool cost delta ~ 12-15% on monthly GPU spend for your projected qps, but it brought TTFT into your SLA.

[07:05] Ethan Cole: what about fallback strategies during capacity spikes? e.g., if Dedicated is saturated, can we failover to a cheaper hosted model?
[07:15] Lena Park: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible variant — e.g., smaller quantized model or hosted fallback with slightly higher token cost but preserve availability. We can set per-route fallback policies.
[07:30] Priya Malhotra: do we lose audit / data residency guarantees when we fallback to hosted?
[07:38] Lena Park: good question — fallback policy can be constrained by data residency or tenancy. For Aurora's compliance, we'd probably restrict fallback to the same region and only to instances that meet your KMS/HSM controls. We'll put that in the SOW.

[08:05] Marcus Li: back to kernels — for long sequences the block-attention kernel reduces compute by ~20% and lowers tail tokens, but it adds a ~40-60ms init on cold workers. There's a trick: keep a small pool of block-kernel warm workers for high-seq requests and route those there.
[08:34] Jordan Reyes: routing complexity seems fine as long as router is deterministic and visible in tracing.
[08:40] Lena Park: Console tracing will show per-route model variant and kernel used.

[09:05] Speaker 3: (inaudible)

[10:00] Marcus Li: proposed experiments this week: 1) microbench TTFT with seq=[48,128,256], streaming on/off, batching windows [6,8,12ms]; 2) warm pool size sensitivity; 3) kernel routing test (keep 2 warm block-kernel workers). I'll run these and upload results.
[10:20] Priya Malhotra: great. can you also try a run with quantization q4_0 vs q4_1 for our medium seq bucket?
[10:27] Marcus Li: yes will add that.

[11:00] Jordan Reyes: on the sample traces — we've anonymized and removed PII, i'll upload a 1k-request subset by friday. should be representative: median 48, mean 112, tail to 512.
[11:12] Ethan Cole: i'll coordinate on S3 access.

[12:00] Lena Park: any blockers on platform side, Priya?
[12:06] Priya Malhotra: just procurement timelines; we need pricing to sign. also legal asked for SOC2 attestation and encryption details.
[12:18] Lena Park: understood — i'll send the updated SOW + pricing for Dedicated pilot and include SOC2 docs.

[13:05] Marcus Li: one subtle note — with streaming enabled we observed some micro-oscillation in request latency when mixture of long/short sequences present; we mitigated with size-based batching and that smoothed it. will show numbers in the sheet.
[13:30] Jordan Reyes: that's exactly what we saw in our internal traces; streaming improves perceived latency but needs careful batching heuristics.

[15:00] Lena Park: ok let's recap next steps. Marcus to run benchmarks and share sheet by 2026-10-15; Lena to send SOW and SOC2 docs by 2026-10-18; Jordan/Ethan to upload anonymized traces by 2026-10-16.
[15:18] Priya Malhotra: good, and let's tentatively meet same time next week.
[15:24] Ethan Cole: okay thanks everyone.
[15:30] Lena Park: thanks all — end call.

Action Items (auto-extract): Marcus to run microbench (TTFT + streaming + quant profiles); Lena to send SOW/pricing and SOC2 link; Jordan/Ethan to provide traces.

Notes: transcription has a few mislabels and low audio bits; see perf sheet for raw numbers.
